faction.pirates.name: Pirates
faction.pirates.desc: Seafaring tech raiders who scavenge lost code fragments from the Digital Chaos. They excel at improvisation and quick thinking.
faction.pirates.bonus: Extra card flips in memory puzzles (+{count})
faction.scholars.name: Scholars
faction.scholars.desc: Keepers of ancient algorithms who study the Codex methodically. They value precision and deep understanding.
faction.mercenaries.name: Mercenaries
faction.mercenaries.desc: Battle-hardened code warriors who tackle any challenge for the right price. They thrive under time pressure.

concept.docker.name: Docker
concept.docker.definition: Packages an app and its dependencies into an isolated container.
concept.docker.hint: Docker helps the same app run consistently on different computers.
concept.git.name: Git
concept.git.definition: Tracks code changes so teams can review and restore earlier versions.
concept.git.hint: Git records snapshots called commits and keeps work in a repository.
concept.github.name: GitHub
concept.github.definition: Hosts Git repositories and tools for sharing and reviewing code.
concept.github.hint: Teams use GitHub to collaborate on projects stored with Git.
concept.api.name: API
concept.api.definition: A defined way for software programs to request data or actions.
concept.api.hint: An API is like a menu that tells another program what it can ask for.
concept.rest.name: REST
concept.rest.definition: A web API style that uses standard HTTP requests and resources.
concept.rest.hint: REST APIs commonly use requests such as GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.
concept.kubernetes.name: Kubernetes
concept.kubernetes.definition: Automates the deployment and scaling of containerized apps.
concept.kubernetes.hint: Kubernetes can restart containers and spread them across computers.
concept.sql.name: SQL
concept.sql.definition: A language for reading and changing data in relational tables.
concept.sql.hint: SQL queries can find, add, update, or remove rows in a database.
concept.nosql.name: NoSQL
concept.nosql.definition: A family of databases built for flexible, non-table data.
concept.nosql.hint: NoSQL databases can store data as documents, key-value pairs, or graphs.
concept.cicd.name: CI/CD
concept.cicd.definition: Automatically tests, builds, and delivers code changes.
concept.cicd.hint: CI/CD pipelines help teams catch problems and ship updates often.
concept.container.name: Container
concept.container.definition: A lightweight isolated package that runs an application.
concept.container.hint: A container includes an app and runs separately from other apps.
concept.image.name: Image
concept.image.definition: A reusable template used to create a container.
concept.image.hint: An image contains the files and setup needed to start a container.
concept.branch.name: Branch
concept.branch.definition: An independent line of work in a version-control project.
concept.branch.hint: A branch lets you make changes without altering the main line of work.
concept.commit.name: Commit
concept.commit.definition: A saved snapshot of changes in a version-control project.
concept.commit.hint: A commit records a set of changes with a message describing them.
concept.merge.name: Merge
concept.merge.definition: Combines changes from one branch into another.
concept.merge.hint: After review, a team often merges a finished branch into its main branch.
concept.cache.name: Cache
concept.cache.definition: Stores frequently used data for faster future access.
concept.cache.hint: A cache saves a copy nearby so software can avoid slow repeat work.
concept.server.name: Server
concept.server.definition: A computer or program that provides services to other devices.
concept.server.hint: A server waits for requests and sends back data or other results.
concept.cloud.name: Cloud
concept.cloud.definition: Computing services delivered over the internet.
concept.cloud.hint: Cloud services let you use remote computers, storage, and software.
concept.terminal.name: Terminal
concept.terminal.definition: A text-based window for running commands on a computer.
concept.terminal.hint: Type commands in a terminal to work with files and developer tools.
concept.database.name: Database
concept.database.definition: An organized collection of data that software can search.
concept.database.hint: Apps use databases to store information such as accounts and settings.
concept.frontend.name: Frontend
concept.frontend.definition: The part of an app that users see and interact with.
concept.frontend.hint: Buttons, pages, and menus are common parts of a frontend.
